text:
Maya (PM): dropped a fresh set of mocks for autoscale controls — focussed on min/max steppers, a lighter-weight burst flyout, and SLO slider variants. figma: https://figma.redwood/infer/autoscale-v4 :eyes:

Sam (Design): I prototyped a compact layout: pool selector + min/max steppers inline, small 'Burst' chip that opens a right-side flyout. Flyout contains quota + duration + Apply/Cancel. Thoughts?

Kevin (Eng): flyout is 👍. easier to map to allocation API. prefer explicit Apply so backend can validate cost and return errors. also: clamp values server-side and return precise availableCapacity.

Priya (Accessibility): main a11y items: focus management when flyout opens (trap focus), visible focus rings for steppers, and aria-live updates for the SLO slider. color alone can't convey risk.

Sam (Design): good call — I'll add a patterned fill to the SLO rail + an icon (shield/warning) to the slider thumb state. Also adding a tiny "Est. cost" line under the steppers that updates while editing.

Liam (Data): estimator can return a quick ballpark based on 30-day usage + current token mix. We can show: "Est. cost: $6.80/hr (+9%)". If data missing, show a cached/caution state.

Kevin (Eng): implementation notes: debounce estimator calls to 400ms, fall back to cached estimate if pricing service times out, show small banner: "Estimates may be delayed". telemetry: autoscale.preview with pool_id, min, max.

Maya (PM): copy question: guardrail messaging currently says "Guardrail prevents extreme configs". I want something clearer and less alarming. Options: A) "Automatic guardrails limit risky configs to protect SLOs and costs." B) "Guardrails protect your SLOs and costs." Which is better?

Priya (Accessibility): A is clearer for screen readers (more context). Add a "Why?" tooltip link that reads the rationale. Also label icons with accessible names.

Sam (Design): agree A. I'll keep a short sentence then the 'Why?' tooltip. Tooltip to include examples: "e.g., min > pool capacity, burst pushes you above quota".

Kevin (Eng): edge cases to handle: 1) user sets min close to capacity + enables burst -> show inline validation error and disable Apply. 2) concurrent edits -> server returns conflict diff; show a small banner: "Config changed upstream — refresh or merge" with a diff preview.

Priya (Accessibility): keyboard flow suggestion: Tab order -> Pool picker -> Min stepper -> Max stepper -> Burst chip -> SLO slider -> Details. When flyout opens, focus to first input and `aria-expanded="true"` on chip. Return focus on close. Ensure stepper buttons are 44x44 touch size.

Sam (Design): about steppers: default increments = 1 GPU, but show a tiny toggle for fractional when pool supports (0.5). If fractional not supported, show disabled state with tooltip. Copy for step labels: use "Minimum reserved" and "Maximum (burst cap)"? Thoughts?

Maya (PM): avoid renaming min/max too much — keep concise: "Min reserved" and "Max (burst)" with helper text beneath. We want to be precise but not confusing.

Liam (Data): optional: include a small sparkline of recent utilization near the pool name to help choose min. Could be tiny and low-contrast.

Kevin (Eng): sure, but keep it lazy-loaded. Also server validation rules: ensure min <= max, and (currentReserved + burstQuota) <= poolCapacity, else return field errors. Add an API error code for conflict: 409 + payload {currentConfig, attemptedConfig}.

Priya (Accessibility): SLO slider announcements: when changed, post to aria-live polite: e.g., "SLO target set to 99% — may increase cost by approximately 20 percent." Also expose exact numeric percent change in the live region.

Sam (Design): will mock patterned SLO states, add icon labels, add estimator line, and update guardrail copy to the suggested A. I'll also include a small link text "Why this?" opening an accessible tooltip.

mockup-bot: new frame uploaded to figma (autoscale/v4) — Sam annotated focus states and flyout behavior.

Maya (PM): next steps: Sam to iterate on mocks (add patterns + estimator), Kevin to scope server changes (validation, estimator debounce, conflict payload), Priya to prepare a11y checklist, Liam to provide estimator baseline. I'll file a short ticket linking this thread.

Kevin (Eng): noted. I'll include unit tests for the conflict and capacity checks.

Priya (Accessibility): I'll review the updated frame once posted and send checklist items inline. Thanks! :raised_hands:
